references.text: Another description of the manna, comparing it to coriander seed and describing how it was prepared and tasted like cakes baked with oil.
Describes how the manna fell over the camp at night along with the dew.
Moses reminds the people that God humbled them and gave them manna to eat, a food they had not known before.
Yet another reminder that God gave them manna in the wilderness, food their ancestors did not know.
The manna ceased the day after the Israelites ate from the produce of the land in Canaan.
Nehemiah mentions that God gave them manna from heaven when they were hungry in the wilderness.
The psalm describes the manna as grain from heaven and bread of angels which God rained down on the people.
The psalm tells how God satisfied the people with bread from heaven when they asked for food.
Jesus refers to the manna that their fathers ate in the wilderness, quoting 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat'.
Jesus compares himself to the manna and calls himself the bread of life that came down from heaven, unlike the manna their fathers ate and yet died.
Mentions the golden jar of manna that was kept in the ark of the covenant as a memorial.
Jesus promises to give the hidden manna to the one who overcomes, a spiritual parallel to the manna in the wilderness.
Complementary descriptions of the appearance of the manna confirming God's specific provision.
